claim_under_test: An instruction arm with no experience, no search, no model and no parameters can be moved off two failures the refusal census could not see, because they are not vocabulary gaps: (a) the page grades on a press the sentence never names, and (b) the sentence names a COORDINATE inside a widget rather than a control. Neither is fixed by adding words to a compiler.
corrections: The 'drag pages dispatch without registering reward' note was wrong about the cause. drag-box moved the box to exactly the right place ([94,86,28,28] inside [73,75,58,58]) and had no way to say 'Submit'; drag-cube is won by a bare Submit because its layout starts correct.
The label LABEL_NOT_ON_THE_PAGE was true of the OBSERVATION and false of the page on all three click-tab-2 pages: `Quis` was in the third tab's panel, reachable, and the arm had no name for a tab.

The 11/10/2016 pages did NOT need a locale. The picker writes back `12/05/2016` when a day is chosen, and pressing a day above 12 makes that literal unambiguous -- the page declares its own field order.
The first cut of the picker keyed three case-variants of the same word into one list, counted one December as two, and answered AMBIGUOUS on the first real page.

The existing test test_executes_only_what_it_fully_understood caught the implied ending firing on a HALF-understood instruction and pressing Submit over unfinished work. The arm was fixed, not the test.
honest_limits: AUTHORITY NONE -- one producer run in one sandbox, not independent verification.
66/130 is these 130 pages at three seeds with a 30-action budget. Not a benchmark claim, not a family rank.
The 17 pages that are executed-and-lost still fail; the 8 HALF_UNDERSTOOD pages name a part of the sentence that is still not compiled. Neither is fixed by this round.
The picker understands dates and times only. It is not a general widget reader, and it refuses rather than guesses when the page shows a part twice.
Nothing here is memory: the ending and the picker answer are derived from (sentence, observation) on every look, and nothing is carried between pages.
laws: A census that reports why the arm DECLINED and not why it STOPPED measures its own optimism.
An action is finished when the page says so, not when the sentence does. The sentence is evidence about the page, not a complete specification of it.
Two legal readings is not ambiguity to be resolved by convention; it is a question the page can be asked.
Half an instruction earns no ending: delivering work that was never done, confidently, is the trace a wrong answer makes.
An index is the bridge's name for an element and a list position is where it sits. They agree until they do not.

measured_effect.reward: read only after the arm stops, and only to record whether it was right

the_wrong_answer_this_replaces: The refusal census. It recorded WHY the arm declined and never why a page it had accepted was lost, so 19 pages that the PAGE failed and 59 that the arm stopped short of were both counted as 'not refused' -- a measurement of its own optimism. Recording the episode's stopping state is what exposed both defects within one turn.
what_was_built: canonical/runtime/implied_ending_v1.py -- the one control that means 'deliver this', pressed only after every act the sentence named is done

canonical/runtime/picker_answer_v1.py -- a date read as components; the widget's STATE read (which month is shown) before any part is answered; a probe that makes the page declare its own notation when the sentence is genuinely ambiguous
SELECT_PICKER operator + _check_select_picker -- judged on the field's own value, never on which elements were pressed
EXPAND re-finds its headers every page by 'still shut', because indices renumber when a section opens
_reveal: a tab is a container; the walk steps through sections of an exclusive accordion instead of re-pressing the first
two ledgers in the arm -- 'pressed at all' and 'pressed THE TARGET' -- because one press of a step retired a FIND clause
_first_matching(prefer_own_word=True) -- a container whose subtree contains the target is not the target
_label_at by index, not by list position
